title: NSS Feed Output Format: Admin Audit Logs

blocks.text: The admin audit Nanolog Streaming Service (NSS) feed specifies the data from the admin audit logs that the NSS sends to the security information and event management (SIEM) system. You can configure an NSS feed by including one or more fields. The fields and their values display in the NSS feed output.

blocks.item: View a sample admin audit log.

blocks.text: The following tables display information about the admin audit log fields and possible values for those fields.
The following are date and time fields:

table: The time and date of the transaction. This excludes the time zone.
The time zone. This is the same as the time zone you specified when you configured the NSS feed.
The epoch time of the transaction

blocks.text: The following are admin audit fields:

table: The unique record identifier for each log
The action performed by the admin in the Zscaler Admin Console
The location in the Zscaler Admin Console where the action was performed
The sublocation in the Zscaler Admin Console where the action was performed
The specific location within a subcategory
SSL Rule Name User Object Name
The means by which the user performs their actions
The interface is either the Admin UI or an API

The admin ID. Possible field values include: The login ID of a user from your organization's Internet & SaaS (ZIA) tenant The login ID of a Zscaler partner Zscaler Remote Assistance Service Support (i.e., when a partner accesses your organization’s Internet & SaaS tenant from the Zscaler Management Portal for Partners) Partner Template (i.e., when a Policy Template is created and applied from the Management Portal for Partners to your organization’s Internet & SaaS tenant)

example@zscaler.com example@partner.com Zscaler remote assistance Service support (Applicable only to Management Portal for Partners tenants) Partner Template (Applicable only to Management Portal for Partners tenants)

blocks.text: The Zscaler service hex encodes all non-printable ASCII characters that are in URLs when it sends logs to the NSS. Any URL character that is less than or equal to 0x20, or greater than or equal to 0x7F, is encoded as %HH. This ensures that your SIEM can parse the URLs that contain control characters. For example, a \n character in a URL is encoded as %0A, and a space is encoded as %20.
